d: Stand tall and lift your knees alternately to hip height, swinging the opposite arm forward.
t: Keep your chest up and shoulders relaxed.
Land softly on the ball of each foot.

d: Stand tall and swing both straight arms in big, smooth circles. Reverse the direction halfway.
t: Move from the shoulders, not the wrists.
Keep your neck long and ribs down.

d: Jump your feet apart while raising your arms overhead, then jump back to the start.
t: Land softly with soft knees.
Breathe steadily and keep a light rhythm.

d: Hold a wall for balance and swing one straight leg forward and back in a relaxed, controlled arc.
t: Keep your torso tall; do not lean.
Increase the swing slowly, never force it.

d: Run in place driving each knee up to hip height while pumping your arms.
t: Stay on the balls of your feet.
Drive the knee up, not forward.

d: Jog in place and kick your heels up toward your glutes with each step.
t: Keep your knees pointing down.
Swing your arms like a light jog.

d: Jump with small, quick hops, turning the rope with your wrists and keeping your elbows close to your body.
t: Jump just high enough to clear the rope.
Land softly on the balls of your feet.

d: Sink into a squat, then explode upward into a jump, swinging your arms up. Land softly into the next squat.
t: Keep your chest up and knees over your toes.
Absorb the landing by bending your knees.

d: From a lunge, jump and switch legs in the air, landing softly in a lunge on the other side.
t: Keep your torso tall and your front knee over your ankle.
Start with small jumps and build height over time.

d: Walk fast with long, relaxed strides and swinging arms. Breathe easily.
t: Look ahead, not down.
Roll from heel to toe on every step.

d: Jog at a comfortable pace where you could still hold a conversation.
t: Short, quick steps. Land under your hips.
Relax your hands and shoulders.

d: Run at a strong, steady pace with a slight forward lean and active arms.
t: Stay tall through the hips.
Breathe in a steady rhythm.

d: Run at a fast, controlled pace with a powerful arm drive. Fully recover afterwards.
t: Drive your elbows back hard.
Stay relaxed in the face and shoulders.

d: Grip the bar with straight arms and let your body hang long and relaxed. Let your spine decompress.
t: Relax your shoulders and legs.
Breathe slowly. Come down if your grip fails.

d: Hang from the bar and slowly lift your knees toward your chest, then lower with control.
t: Do not swing. Lift with your abs.
Keep your shoulders active.

d: Lie face down, place your hands under your shoulders and gently press your chest up while your hips stay on the floor.
t: Keep your neck long; look slightly forward.
Stop if you feel any pain in your lower back.

d: Sit back on your heels, reach your arms forward along the floor and let your back lengthen.
t: Breathe deep into your back.
Relax your forehead toward the floor.

d: On hands and knees, slowly round your back while tucking your chin, then arch gently while looking forward.
t: Move one vertebra at a time.
Keep your hands under your shoulders.

d: Lie on your back, hug your knees toward your chest and gently rock to release your lower back.
t: Keep your head and shoulders relaxed.
Breathe out as you pull your knees in.

d: Lie on your back and reach your arms overhead and your toes away. Lengthen your whole body like a rubber band.
t: Press your lower back gently to the floor.
Inhale as you stretch, exhale as you relax.

d: Rest on your forearms and toes with your body in one straight line from head to heels. Squeeze your abs and glutes.
t: Do not let your hips sag or rise.
Breathe steadily and keep your neck neutral.

d: From a high plank, drive your knees toward your chest one after the other at a steady pace.
t: Keep your hips level and shoulders over your hands.
Move fast but stay in control.

d: Squat down, kick your feet back to a plank, return to a squat and jump up with your arms overhead.
t: Keep your core tight in the plank.
Land softly and reset your breathing.

d: Stand with your back against a wall and slide your arms up and down like a snow angel, keeping contact with the wall.
t: Keep your lower back, head and arms touching the wall.
Move slowly and do not shrug your shoulders.

d: Stand with your heels, hips, shoulders and head against the wall. Gently tuck your chin and grow tall.
t: Imagine a string pulling the top of your head upward.
Keep your ribs down and breathe slowly.

d: Raise your arms overhead and rise onto your toes, stretching as tall as you can. Lower slowly and repeat.
t: Reach through your fingertips.
Keep your core tight to avoid arching your back.

d: Lie on your back with arms up and knees bent. Lower the opposite arm and leg slowly, keeping your lower back pressed down.
t: Move slowly. Exhale as you extend.
Do not let your back arch off the floor.

d: On hands and knees, extend one arm forward and the opposite leg back. Hold briefly, then switch sides.
t: Keep your hips level, as if balancing a glass of water.
Reach long instead of high.

d: Lie face down with arms forward. Lift your arms, chest and legs a few centimeters off the floor and hold.
t: Look at the floor to keep your neck neutral.
Squeeze your glutes and lower back gently.

d: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat. Lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
t: Push through your heels.
Squeeze your glutes at the top.

d: Step one leg back with the heel on the floor and press your hands against a wall. Bend the front knee to feel the stretch.
t: Keep the back heel on the floor.
Keep your back leg straight.

d: Stand on one leg, pull your other heel toward your glute and keep your knees together. Hold for balance.
t: Keep your knees close together.
Stand tall and do not arch your back.

d: Kneel in a lunge, tuck your pelvis and gently push your hips forward. Raise your arms for a deeper stretch.
t: Squeeze the glute of the back leg.
Keep your chest tall.

d: Sit with your legs straight, then fold forward from the hips and reach toward your toes. Keep your back long.
t: Hinge from the hips, not the back.
Relax your neck and breathe out as you fold.

d: Stand with feet hip-width apart, reach both arms overhead and bend gently to one side, then the other.
t: Keep both feet flat on the floor.
Lengthen up before you bend over.

d: Stand tall, bring your straight arms behind your back and lift them gently while opening your chest.
t: Pull your shoulder blades toward each other.
Keep your chin level.

d: Sit or stand tall. Glide your head straight back, as if making a gentle double chin, and hold. Keep your eyes level.
t: Do not tilt your head down.
Feel the stretch at the base of your skull.

d: Place your tongue on the roof of your mouth and open slowly, only as far as is comfortable. Close with control.
t: Open in a straight line with no clicking.
Stop if you feel pain or hear popping.

d: Place your fist under your chin and open your mouth slowly against gentle resistance. Hold, then release.
t: Use light pressure only.
Keep your head still and your shoulders relaxed.

d: Tilt your ear toward your shoulder and let the weight of your head stretch the side of your neck. Switch sides.
t: Keep your opposite shoulder down.
Do not pull with your hand.

d: Slowly lower your chin toward your chest and feel a gentle stretch along the back of your neck. Return slowly.
t: Keep your shoulders relaxed.
Do not bounce or force the stretch.

d: Rest your whole tongue lightly on the roof of your mouth, teeth almost touching and lips closed. Breathe through your nose.
t: Do not press hard. Keep it light.
Stay tall with your head balanced over your shoulders.

d: With two fingers, make slow circles on the muscle of your cheek near the jaw. Use gentle pressure.
t: Breathe out as you massage.
Keep your jaw relaxed and teeth slightly apart.
